decisions.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
decisions.abstract: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $\Delta V(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{N\Delta V(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we check it against mean extinction times obtained without the action solver, i.e., from the backward equation of the jump process on a truncated lattice and from exact stochastic simulation. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $\Delta V(r)=\Delta V_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $\Delta V_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first, and at $r=1$ the barrier is 55% larger than $\Delta V_\infty$. A formal first-order expansion attributes this increase to the lag of the signal, of which the fluctuations of the signal remove a quarter. The saddle barrier $\Delta V(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, whereas the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply, by paths which keep the signal high and are usually followed by recovery. The mean extinction times of the backward equation, which include failed attempts, have a prefactor which tends to a constant, and they grow at a rate within $10^{-5}$ of $\Delta V(r)$ at every tested rate.

decisions.title: Critical Free-Energy Variance in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
decisions.abstract: We study the variance of the free energy in the Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at zero external field. For every system size and inverse temperature $\beta>0$, we prove $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(\beta) \le \log\chi+(\beta^2-1)(\chi-1), \chi=N\mathbb{E}\langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle_\beta$, where $R_{1,2}$ is the replica overlap and $F_N^{\mathrm{off}}=N^{-1}\log Z_N^{\mathrm{off}}$ omits diagonal disorder. The proof uses an exact identity for the edges incident to one spin, Schur complements, and Gaussian disorder interpolation. At criticality the bound reduces to $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(1)\le\log\chi$. An explicit nonnegative integral measures its gap. A second decomposition relates this gap to a mixed cubic overlap functional. Existing moment and cavity estimates imply that its required integral is bounded. Critical susceptibility asymptotics give the sharp logarithmic upper coefficient and show that the gap converges exactly when the variance has a constant term. We extend an entropy bound throughout bounded critical temperature windows and establish overlap moment stability on a smaller interval.

decisions.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
decisions.abstract: We present a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals from autonomous scattering and reflection data. Spatial homogeneity forces the spectral labels of right- and left-moving particles to be affine with a common slope, so bulk and boundary couplings sample one spectral trajectory. A complete round trip shifts the spectral labels and gives boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations provide local consistency, while boundary-qKZ flatness provides global consistency. We reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by Cayley inversion of the bulk and boundary matching matrices. We apply the construction to rational $SU(N)$ scattering with fundamental boundary impurities and to an $O(3)$ model with a spin-$\tfrac12$ impurity. For the $SU(2)$ impurity, we construct explicit boundary-qKZ solutions as lattice sums of off-shell boundary Bethe vectors and recover the static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes

decisions.title: Geometric heat pumping on a quantum processor
decisions.abstract: Geometric heat pumping is the transfer of energy between reservoirs at equal temperature where the heat exchanged in an adiabatic cycle depends only on the driving contour in parameter space. We implement this mechanism on a superconducting quantum processor using a collision model, where a driven qubit interacts repeatedly with two ancilla qubits that are prepared in thermal states and emulate the reservoirs. Energy measurements before and after each interaction provide a calorimetric record of the heat exchanged with each reservoir. By reversing the driving contour, we extract a heat contribution associated with pumping. Its dependence on the period and on the contour follows exact simulations of the collision model, without adjustable parameters, and approaches in the slow-driving regime the geometric limit of the corresponding Lindblad dynamics.

decisions.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
decisions.abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

decisions.title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
decisions.abstract: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

decisions.title: Photon-stimulated decay of $χ$-matched ancillas causes unheralded bit flips in bosonic codes
decisions.abstract: Bosonic codes often read out their syndrome with a transmon ancilla whose computational levels $g$ and $f$ have equal parity and matched dispersive shifts: a decay $f\to e$ is then heralded and leaves the code intact, while the direct $f\to g$ is forbidden by parity. We show that the photons of the code open this decay at first order in the ancilla's decay rate. Dressing by the code mode lets the charge noise that limits the ancilla's $T_1$ drive a photon-stimulated Raman decay $|f,n\rangle\to|g,n+1\rangle$, at $(n+1)(\chi_{ge}/2g_{01})^2$ times the $f\to e$ rate for a smooth noise spectrum. When the matching is set by the detuning, the decay costs $\approx\Gamma_{fe}/\alpha$ per gate and photon, whatever the coupling strength; a deliberate mismatch or matching by a drive lowers this cost, and a qubit ancilla has no such channel. The opened decay is unheralded and flips a cat with probability $\approx 1/2$; being first order, it overtakes the second-order double decay $f\to e\to g$ as the ancilla improves. In a microscopic model of the Ocelot repetition cat code, it makes the bit-flip floor of the gates grow linearly with the cat size, by a factor 1.2-1.7 from four to ten photons, which would limit the noise bias to $\sim 10^3$. The published gate data end at four photons and do not yet test this growth.
